title: Your story and what you say no to
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Can you tell your story in a way that is simple, relevant and repeatable?

I said: ask what in your story indicates success, why they need you and what you will do in the customer's life. I said every story has good and evil and a hero, and that in your story you are the one who will fix the problem and empower the person.
I gave exercises: write your story; analyze each of your social media and summarize your image; write a paragraph about who you are now in front of people and who you want to be.
I said that one of my rules is three things about your messaging: simplicity, relevance and repeatability. It must be simple, relevant and repeatable.

I said that one example from a student of an online butcher's videos shows how appealing to the senses and the anticipation of the taste carried the message. The student said he would be cautious: he may like the person's story but not his model or behavior.

A student said: branding is also what you do not do. I said that is an important part, and that the ability to say no gives you the freedom to choose who you want to be, though I still struggle with it. I said there is a thin line between no, that is not what I do, and yes, I need to adapt and take risks.
What is the one sentence about you that people will repeat?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your story in one paragraph.
Write where you are the hero for the customer.
Write your message in one simple, relevant, repeatable line.
Write what you say no to.
Write your social media image in a paragraph.

check.q: What three words did I give for messaging?
What did a student say branding is also about?
What did I say saying no gives you?
choices: The freedom to choose who you want to be

recap: Tell your story simply. Know what you say no to.
